artifacts.summary: Rules on the execution-half gap: adopts (c) -- a short generic obligation in checkpoint-commit.md (pointer, not copy, into general-implementation-agent.md) plus a minimal non-blocking backstop call to the already-built derived_probe_run_all from git-commit-phase.sh -- and flags, re-derived live, that neither half has any effect on the real BimodalLogic incident without a companion consumer-repo task declaring coupled_generated_surfaces there.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system's checkpoint-commit.md/git-commit-phase.sh staging pipeline stages only what the agent self-reports in files_touched/modified_files; nothing re-runs a generator before staging. The Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check additionally DROPS any staged path not already inside the task's declared file_scope -- so even a dutiful, un-prompted regeneration by an implementing agent is silently undone at commit time unless the regenerated path is already declared in file_scope. The execution half (re-run+stage) and the declaration half (file_scope membership) are coupled at this exact site.

Two distinct repo-level declaration schemas exist in .claude-extensions.json for generated-artifact staleness: derived_artifact_probes (a build-free check_command + derived_output_dirs, read at implement-postflight, blocking) and coupled_generated_surfaces (trigger_glob + generated_paths + commit_blocking, read only at plan-acceptance time by an inline helper in validate-artifact.sh, purely advisory). coupled_generated_surfaces is pure glob/string matching with zero command execution -- cheaper and more precisely source-correlated than derived_artifact_probes' check_command. Its documentation already names a second consumer as the trigger to promote the inline helper to scripts/lib/; wiring it into git-commit-phase.sh against actual files_touched (rather than only the plan's declared prose) would be that second consumer, and would also be the first place commit_blocking could become a real refusal rather than inert warning-text metadata.

anchor-pointer-convention.md (agent-system core, created 2026-11-05) requires a block restated across files to collapse to a one-line pointer naming the anchor's path+heading rather than a verbatim copy; lint-anchor-pointer-collapse.sh only polices files already registered in lint/collapsed-blocks/registry.tsv as collapsed-FROM, so it does not catch a freshly hand-duplicated paragraph added to two files at once -- that regression has to be avoided by authoring discipline (write the pointer form from the start), not caught by this lint after the fact.
